result.title: Drift-adaptive Representation Preservation for Domain-Incremental Learning
result.summary: Pretrained vision models provide strong general-purpose representations, but in Domain-Incremental Learning (DIL), where the input distribution changes sequentially, adapting to new domains often degrades performance on previously learned ones. We observe that forgetting is not uniform across domains and classes and is not explained by training order alone. This motivates us to track each past domain-class concept individually. We use representation drift, defined as the deviation of a past concept's current representation from a fixed anchor, as a measurable surrogate for forgetting risk. The measured drift then serves two complementary roles. A consolidation loss assigns stronger preservation to high-drift pairs, while prototype construction down-weights highly drifted domains to reduce their influence on the class reference. Preservation is thus allocated by measured drift rather than assumed importance. To obtain this signal during training without storing past raw data, we repurpose a Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (JEPA). For each domain-class pair, we store only a compact context summary in the backbone feature space and rerun it through the learned context-to-target relation to measure its drift from the fixed anchor. Across DomainNet, Office-Home, CORe50, and CDDB-Hard, our method sustains a strong accuracy-forgetting balance on every benchmark, using substantially less training memory than accuracy-competitive methods and the smallest storage among compared methods.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究域增量学习中的遗忘问题：按「域-类」概念分别追踪其表示相对固定锚点的漂移量，把漂移当作遗忘风险的可测代理，用它同时调节保持损失强度与原型构建权重；为在不保存旧数据的情况下获得该信号，改造 JEPA，仅存紧凑上下文摘要并重跑上下文到目标的关系来重算漂移。
AI.relevance_reason: 以预测架构重算表示相对锚点的漂移并据此分配保持力度，可能可供核查 LVR 中 latent 状态漂移、表示坍缩的监测与训练期监督分配；但该工作面向纯视觉分类的持续学习，未涉及多模态推理。
